newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse ends lower, pace of fall slows.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse ends lower, pace of fall slows.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed but the BUX index ended lower on Tuesday as the Budapest bourse moved in line with the price trends on most major and central European bourses, traders said.
They gave no indication that the upgrading of Hungary's debts by Standard & Poor's on Monday would have an immediate influence on the domestic equities market.
The Budapest bourse was seen approaching its bottom and was expected to rebound, traders said, but they emphasised that this market could not move independently from global trends.
The BUX index closed at 3,517.39 points, down 8.00.
"International trends are mixed, indices move mostly down, and we cannot make ourselves independent from this," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
BUX index futures ended mixed on Tuesday, closing higher by 30.50 to 31.00 points for three maturities, remaining steady for two, and slipping nine points for one maturity, bourse figures showed.
On Tuesday all pharmaceuticals shares strengthened but traders said this did not cause much surprise.
"(A rise) by Egis could be expected as it has fallen 19 percent within a month," Berecz said.
"Speculative buyers have appeared and the same was true for Richter," he said.
Egis ended at 9,100 forints, up 100. Richter finished at 8,250 forints, up 150. Human closed at 2,740, up 20.

Oil and gas company MOL slipped five forints to close at 1,545 forints following the official opening of the 117 kilometre long Hungarian-Austrian gas (HAG) pipeline, which was built by MOL and Austria's OMV.
